# @sanity/workflow-cli

## 0.37.0

### Minor Changes

- 6304d4a: `sanity-workflows start` and the instance commands (`fire-action`, `abort`, `set-stage`, `reset-activity`, `diagnose`, and the diagnosis in `show`) now accept runtime-supplied refs to any resource the deployment binds in `resourceAliases`, in another dataset or another project. A release or subject ref outside the workflow resource no longer fails with `RefResourceUndeclaredError` when its resource is bound. Clients for the bound resources reuse the CLI's existing token and API host, so that one login must be a member of every bound project. A ref to a resource the deployment does not bind still fails with `RefResourceUndeclaredError`.

  `@sanity/workflow-engine` exports `deploymentResourceClients({client, deployment})`, which builds the same `resourceClients` resolver from a deployment's `resourceAliases` and any client with `withConfig`, for hosts other than the CLI.

  **No upgrade action required.** To start a workflow whose content lives in another dataset or project, add that resource to the deployment's `resourceAliases` in `sanity.workflow.ts`; the definition does not need to reference the alias.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI reference and configuration guide where they say the CLI admits runtime refs to the workflow resource only, the declared resource surface section of the engine reference, and the cross-dataset setup guidance; document `deploymentResourceClients` in the engine API reference.

- b76627b: The Workflows CLI now finds `sanity.workflow.ts` (or `.js`/`.mjs`) from any subdirectory of your project, the same way the `sanity` and `sanity blueprints` CLIs find their config. It looks in the working directory, then in each parent directory, and uses the first config it finds. Every command that reads the config also accepts `--path`, which names a config file directly, or a directory to start the upward search from. `blueprints generate` writes, and `deploy` checks, the generated Blueprint files next to the config file, not in the directory you ran the command from. Telemetry reports `--path` by name only, never its value.

  **No upgrade action required.** A command run from the directory that holds the config behaves as before. A command run from a directory without one now uses the nearest parent's config instead of failing.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI configuration section and command reference to describe the upward search, the `--path` flag, and where generated Blueprint files are written.

- b5a24c0: The Workflows CLI's topics are now plural, matching the Sanity CLI's own topics such as `datasets`, `documents`, and `blueprints`: `sanity workflows definitions list | show | diff | delete | validate` and `sanity workflows blueprints generate`. The singular `definition` and `blueprint` still run the same commands as hidden aliases with no warning, so existing scripts and CI jobs keep working. Help, examples, and suggested next commands print the plural form. Generated Blueprint files keep their existing `Generated by` header, so `blueprints generate --check` and `deploy` report no drift after upgrading. A telemetry logger you supply through `sanity.workflow.ts` now receives `commandArguments` such as `['definitions', 'list']`, whichever spelling was typed.

  **No upgrade action required.** Switch scripts and docs to `definitions` and `blueprints` when convenient. If you filter your own telemetry on `commandArguments`, match the plural topics as well as the singular ones.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI command reference, guides, and examples that show `definition …` or `blueprint generate` to the plural `definitions …` and `blueprints generate`, and mention that the singular still works.

- 8196fbe: The needs report printed by `sanity-workflows blueprints generate` is shorter and lists facts only: which functions are generated and what each runs. It no longer prints trigger filters or how the heartbeat works. The heartbeat line reads "a scheduled function ticks deadlines each minute, subject to plan cadence, and re-queues effects no drain picked up", adjusted to what the deployment needs.

  **No upgrade action required**, unless a script parses the report's lines; update it to the new wording.

  **Docs impact:** Replace the example report in the CLI guide's blueprint generation section, which now keeps the prerequisites and the drift check only.

- ae64320: The Workflows CLI's read commands (`list`, `show`, `tail`, `diagnose`, `definitions list`, and `definitions show`) can now inspect one resource you name, with or without a `sanity.workflow.ts`. They take the Sanity CLI's own targeting flags: `--project-id <id>` and `--dataset <name>` (`-p` and `-d`) together for a dataset, or `--media-library-id <id>` for a media library. With these flags the CLI loads no config and reads only that resource, so they can't be combined with `--deployment` or `--path`; `--partition` still filters. Commands that write keep acting through a deployment in `sanity.workflow.ts` and don't accept these flags. `list`'s help no longer says it reads "the configured dataset".

  **No upgrade action required.** Without the new flags, every command reads the resources `sanity.workflow.ts` declares, as before.

  **Docs impact:** Add the targeting flags to the CLI reference for the six read commands, and to the guide that explains how reads choose their resources, including that write commands still need a config.

- 9ec15d6: `sanity-workflows deploy` now warns before deploying to the
  `default` partition of a workflow resource whose definitions are all in
  other partitions. This is what happens when an upgrade deletes a
  deployment's `tag` instead of renaming it to `partition`: the deploy would
  target `default`, and the workflows in the old partition would disappear
  from that deployment. The warning names the partitions that hold
  definitions and the `partition` value to set. In an interactive terminal,
  `deploy` then asks whether to continue: Enter continues, and answering no
  exits before anything is written. A `--dry-run` or a non-interactive run, such as CI, prints the
  warning and continues.

  `@sanity/workflow-engine` now exports `DEFAULT_PARTITION`, the partition
  name (`'default'`) a deployment uses when it omits `partition`.

  **No upgrade action required.** Deployments that set `partition`, and
  resources where `default` already has definitions, behave as before.

  **Docs impact:** Add the warning and confirmation to the CLI `deploy`
  reference, and to the `tag` → `partition` upgrade guidance as the check
  that catches a deleted `tag`.

- cbf4180: `sanity-workflows deploy` now prints a one-line-per-deployment
  summary of the Sanity Functions the selected deployments need when no
  generated runtime sits beside the config, instead of the full needs report.
  The summary counts each deployment's effect drains, heartbeats, and start
  watchers, and the hint that follows still names `blueprints generate` on every
  run. Both cover only the deployments the run selects: a `--deployment` whose
  definitions need no functions prints nothing about the runtime, even when
  another deployment in the config does.

  `deploy --verbose` prints the full needs report in place of the summary, so
  the report can be read without `blueprints generate` writing a tree. Nothing
  is written to disk in either mode. In a terminal, the report and the hint
  now wrap to the terminal's width with each line's indent kept on its
  continuation lines, in both `deploy` and `blueprints generate`; piped output
  is not wrapped.

  **Upgrade action:** a script that parses the full needs report from `deploy`
  output must add `--verbose` to keep receiving it. Interactive use needs no
  change.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI `deploy` reference where it quotes the
  runtime-needs output, and add `--verbose` to the flag list.

- 3594e60: **BREAKING:** `computeDiffEntries` in `@sanity/workflow-engine` now takes a full `WorkflowClient` instead of a client with only `fetch`. Any `@sanity/client` instance already satisfies it. A caller passing a fetch-only object stops compiling, and a client without `request` throws at runtime when a definition references project roles; pass the real client.

  `sanity-workflows deploy --dry-run` now runs every check a real deploy runs before its first write: structural validation, the reader-floor acknowledgement, the project role catalog check, and spawn-contract and dependency ordering. A batch that references a role the project does not have, or a spawn reference a deploy would reject, fails the dry run with the same error the deploy prints. The dry run also prints the non-blocking warnings the deploy would print beneath each definition, such as a referenced role with no current holder, and `DiffEntry` carries them as `warnings`. Diff entries come back in deploy order, children before parents.

  CLI users have **no upgrade action**. A dry run that used to pass and now fails names a definition the real deploy was already rejecting.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI deploy reference where it describes `--dry-run` as a preview, so it states that the dry run rejects the same batches a deploy rejects, and the engine API reference for `computeDiffEntries` for the client requirement.

- e3ae1ab: **BREAKING:** Code that addresses a workflow deployment uses `partition`
  instead of `tag`. `createEngine`, the SDK and Studio adapter hooks,
  `createBench`, raw workflow verb arguments, MCP tool inputs, and the MCP
  `createWorkflowEngine` address reject `tag`.
  Anyone calling these APIs directly is affected. Until you replace
  `tag: 'prod'` with `partition: 'prod'`, each call throws a migration error
  before any read or write. Upgrade the runtime packages together, pass
  `partition`, and read `engine.partition` / `bench.partition` instead of `.tag`.
  Keep the exact existing value: omitting a non-default value targets different
  data.

  Update these renamed code APIs at the same time:
  - Engine: `validateTag` → `validatePartition`, `tagScopeFilter` →
    `partitionScopeFilter`, `deployedTagsGroq` → `deployedPartitionsGroq`,
    `definitionTagsGroq` → `definitionPartitionsGroq`, and `StartScope.tag` →
    `StartScope.partition`.
  - Test bench: `BENCH_TAG` → `BENCH_PARTITION` and `CreateBenchOptions.tag` →
    `CreateBenchOptions.partition`.
  - MCP: the discovery tool is `workflows_list_partitions` and returns
    `{partitions: [...]}`. The exports `LIST_WORKFLOW_TAGS_TOOL_NAME`,
    `LIST_WORKFLOW_TAGS_DESCRIPTION`, and `WORKFLOW_TAG_DESCRIPTION` are now
    `LIST_WORKFLOW_PARTITIONS_TOOL_NAME`, `LIST_WORKFLOW_PARTITIONS_DESCRIPTION`,
    and `WORKFLOW_PARTITION_DESCRIPTION`. `workflowAddressFromInput` returns
    `partition`.
  - Blueprint runtime (`@sanity/workflow-blueprint/runtime`): `createRuntime`
    requires the deployment `name`; a hand-built deployment object must add the
    configured `name` beside `partition`.
  - CLI: display-row JSON uses `partition`. `list`, `show`, `tail`,
    `definitions list`, and `definitions show` accept `--deployment`, exclusive
    with `--partition`. When an instance ID or definition name is found in
    several deployments, an interactive terminal prompts for one; with `--json`
    or in a non-interactive shell the command fails naming each candidate as
    `name (dataset)` and asks for `--deployment` instead of `--partition`.
    Scripts that matched the old "pass --partition" message should pass
    `--deployment`.

  Content Lake `tag` fields, IDs, references, stored GROQ `$tag` bindings, and
  HTTP request tags stay unchanged. No data migration is needed.

  Configuration you edit rather than call keeps working. A deployment `tag` in
  `sanity.workflow.ts` or `defineWorkflows`, a `tag` in `workflowStudioPlugin`
  options, and the `--tag` / `--all-tags` CLI flags are deprecated. Each
  addresses the same partition and shows a warning naming the replacement: the
  CLI on stderr, the Studio plugin in the browser console, and `defineWorkflows`
  in the console during Blueprint manifest evaluation. The Blueprints provider
  accepts a deprecated deployment `tag` the same way and reports the
  warning in the deploy log. `defineWorkflowConfig` itself prints nothing; it
  returns each message in the new `WorkflowConfig.warnings` array, so code that
  loads a config directly decides where to show them. **No upgrade action required** for
  these yet. Rename them to `partition` (or `--partition` / `--all-partitions`),
  keeping the exact existing value, before the deprecated forms are removed.
  Deleting a `tag` instead of renaming it moves the deployment to the `default`
  partition, where its existing workflows no longer appear. A
  `tag` that is not a string, or that disagrees with an explicit `partition`,
  fails rather than falling back to `default`.

  A deployment you configure in `sanity.workflow.ts` or `defineWorkflows` may
  now omit `partition` when it is alone on its workflow resource, and then uses
  `default`. Multiple deployments on one resource require explicit, distinct
  partitions. `workflowStudioPlugin`'s `partition` is optional too and defaults
  to `default`, and `createRuntime` resolves a deployment that omits it the same
  way. Other code APIs do not: `createEngine`, `useWorkflowEngine` and the other
  adapter hooks, raw verb arguments, and MCP tool inputs still require
  `partition`, and `createBench` uses `BENCH_PARTITION` (`bench`) when you omit
  it. When the plugin finds no
  definitions in its partition, it logs a
  browser console warning naming the partitions that do hold definitions on that
  resource, so a mistyped or forgotten `partition` no longer leaves Studio empty
  without explanation.

  `sanity-workflows blueprints generate` now names each deployment's functions
  and robot token after the deployment `name` instead of its tag (for example
  `wf-prod-runtime` and `wf-prod-start-production-creates` for a deployment named
  `prod`), while runtime scope and filters use `partition`. Upgrade the provider first so it can
  read old serialized state, then regenerate and inspect the Blueprint plan
  before deploying. If a deployment name differs from its old tag, generated
  resources are replaced: plan for the interruption, preserve authored handlers,
  and retire old watchers and schedules.

  **Docs impact:** Update deployment addressing concepts, engine and adapter API
  references (including `WorkflowConfig.warnings`), CLI flags and JSON output
  (including `--deployment` and the ambiguity prompt on the read commands), MCP
  discovery and exported constants, Studio setup examples (the optional
  `partition` and the empty-partition console warning), generated Blueprint
  function names and rollout guidance, and prerelease migration notes using
  `docs/partition-migration.md`.

- bc9c045: `sanity-workflows blueprints generate`, `blueprints generate --check` and `sanity-workflows deploy` now report a stale function directory: a directory under the generated `functions/` tree whose `index.ts` carries the generator's header but which the current definitions no longer produce, such as the directory a renamed start watcher leaves behind. `blueprints generate` lists it with the instruction to remove it. `deploy` prints a warning naming it and continues, because the generated blueprint lists each function by its `src` and does not deploy the directory. A directory whose `index.ts` has no generator header is treated as your own and is never reported.

  `blueprints generate --check` now exits non-zero when a stale function directory is present, naming it, so a CI job that passed before can fail after the upgrade. Remove each directory it names (for example `rm -r functions/wf-prod-start-production-article-review`, left behind when the `article-review` definition, which had a start watcher of its own, is renamed) and the check passes again.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI guide's `blueprints generate` and drift-check sections and the deploy alignment section to describe stale function directories, the `--check` failure, and the deploy warning.

- 9fba4cf: The CLI adds `sanity-workflows definitions validate <file...>`, which checks workflow definitions written as JSON files without a `sanity.workflow.ts` config, a login, or network access. Each file holds one definition or an array of them, in authoring shape or as stored content read back from a deploy. Pass several files to check a parent and its child workflows together. Once every file is read, the command prints one line per valid definition and exits non-zero with every problem listed, path-prefixed, when any definition is invalid. `--json` prints the same `{valid, results}` report the MCP `workflows_validate_definition` tool returns. A file that cannot be read, is not valid JSON, or does not hold definition objects stops the command before validation with a non-zero exit and a text error, with or without `--json`. Use it to run a generate, validate, and fix loop from an agent harness that does not use the Workflows MCP server.

  `@sanity/workflow-engine` exports `validateDefinitionInputs`, the check both the CLI command and the MCP validate tool run, with its `ValidateDefinitionInputResult` and `ValidateDefinitionInputsResult` result types. It covers shape, cross-field rules, and GROQ syntax. Deploy still runs further checks: duplicate names, spawn dependencies, resource bindings, project roles, and the reader-model acknowledgement. The MCP server's `ValidateDefinitionResult` and `ValidateDefinitionsResult` types are now aliases of those engine types, with an unchanged shape.

  **No upgrade action required.** Existing commands, the MCP validate and deploy tools, and `deploy --check` behave as before.

  **Docs impact:** Add `definitions validate` to the CLI command reference, with its JSON-file input and `--json` output. Add `validateDefinitionInputs` to the engine API reference. Mention the command in the definition authoring guide as the validate step for agents that do not use the MCP server.

### Patch Changes

- af41ca9: The Workflows monorepo now uses TypeScript 7 as its default compiler. The
  installed CLI and published workflow declarations continue to work in projects
  using TypeScript 6 or TypeScript 7, including Blueprint generation and
  definition checks. Blueprint generation also works without an installed
  TypeScript package, and the CLI no longer installs a separate TypeScript 6
  compiler for that command.
  The MCP `./stdio` entry can now be loaded from CommonJS through its `require`
  condition.

  **No upgrade action required.** Keep the TypeScript version your project uses.

  **Docs impact:** Update the MCP stdio reference with the CommonJS entry and
  release guidance with the TypeScript 6/7/no-TypeScript compatibility result and
  the CLI dependency change.

- ce08657: When `definitions list`, `list`, or `definitions show` finds nothing, the message now says where the CLI looked: the partition (or `any partition`), the resource, and the deployment when `--deployment` selected it. For example, `no definitions in partition trial-2 of p1.production (deployment my-workflow)` replaces `no definitions found`, so a search scoped to the wrong partition is visible at once. `definitions show` and `show` now report a missing definition or instance as one red `✖` line, like the CLI's other errors, without oclif's `› Error:` framing; both still exit with code 1. `--json` output is unchanged.

  **No upgrade action required.** Scripts that match the old human-readable text (`no definitions found`, `no instances match`) should match the new wording or use `--json`.

  **Docs impact:** None. The CLI docs don't quote these messages.

- 4a561b5: `sanity workflows show --include history` now says what each history row is about. Rows name the stage, activity and action, transition, effect, or field involved, plus the acting user's id, for example `Stage entered: review (by <user-id>)` or `Transition fired: to-review, drafting → review (by <user-id>)`. Forced stage moves read `(forced: <reason>)`, and actions fired automatically read `(triggered)` with no user named. `--json` output is unchanged.

  No upgrade action required.

  **Docs impact: None** — the CLI reference (`docs/reference.md`) lists `show --include history` without example output, so no published text describes the old rows.

- efdddcf: Built-in telemetry from the CLI and the MCP server now includes the sending package's version as `context.packageVersion` on every event, as SDK telemetry already does. This lets analytics count CLI and MCP events by package version. Before this change, the version was sent only as a once-per-session user property (`cliVersion` for the CLI, `packageVersion` for MCP), and per-event analytics did not read it. When the CLI runs inside the Sanity CLI as `sanity workflows`, both the new per-event version and the `cliVersion` user property now report the `@sanity/workflow-cli` version. Previously they reported the Sanity CLI's version.

  **No upgrade action required.** Events from earlier releases still carry no per-event version.

  **Docs impact:** Update the telemetry reference for the CLI and MCP server to list `context.packageVersion` with the other per-event context fields.

- 8b07665: Every next command the Workflows CLI suggests can now be copied and run as
  printed. The `fire-action` action list, the `nuke --instance` abort-first
  refusal, the definition-sharing reminder after `deploy`, and the "run
  `blueprints generate`" hints now start with the binary actually running
  (`sanity-workflows …`, or `sanity workflows …` inside the Sanity CLI) and repeat
  the `--deployment`, `--partition`, or `--all-partitions` selection from the
  current run. A copied hint no longer stops at the deployment picker or fails
  with "Multiple deployments configured".

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact:** Update any CLI guide or reference example that shows the
  `fire-action` list output, the sharing reminder, or the `blueprints generate`
  hint, so the printed commands match the full form, and any page that says the
  commands run only through the standalone `sanity-workflows` binary: they also
  run as `sanity workflows …`, though `sanity --help` does not list them yet.

- 24ef514: The standalone CLI (`npx @sanity/workflow-cli …` or `sanity-workflows …`) no longer prints stack traces when a command is mistyped. An unexpected argument, a missing required argument, or a similar mistake now shows the error and the command's usage, then exits with code 2, the same as under `sanity workflows …`.

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact:** None. The docs don't describe error output for mistyped commands.

- be42dc8: CLI telemetry now records every logged-in run, subject to the existing consent, CI, and `DO_NOT_TRACK` rules. Before, it sent nothing unless a `sanity.workflow.ts` with a dataset-backed deployment was found, so runs that named a resource with `--project-id`/`--dataset` or `--media-library-id`, runs in a directory without a config, and configs with only media library or canvas deployments went unrecorded. Events are attributed to the `--project-id` and `--dataset` a run names, else to the config's first dataset-backed deployment, else to no project; the session's `projectId` and `dataset` properties are left out when no project is known. Events now go to the global Sanity API host instead of the project hostname, as the Sanity CLI's own telemetry does.

  No upgrade action required.

  **Docs impact:** The CLI README's Telemetry section and its session-properties table are updated in this change; no other docs describe when CLI telemetry sends.

- a20e311: The published description of the `Workflows CLI Command Executed` trace now says that each flag used is reported in its canonical long form: an option flag as `--name=value`, and a boolean, redacted, or undeclared flag by its name only. The previous release's changelog note said that the CLI does not send flag values; that note was wrong, and the way the CLI reports flags is unchanged since that release.

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI telemetry reference so its description of `extraArguments` on the `Workflows CLI Command Executed` trace matches the canonical `--name=value` form and lists the flags reported by name only.

- 38ede99: A deploy or dry run that fails now prints its error once. The spinner line names the failure (`Deploy failed` or `Diff failed`) and the message follows it a single time, with no `Error:` framing and no stack trace. Unknown project roles are reported as one line per definition and role, with a reference count and up to five referencing paths, and the message ends with what to do: create the roles in the project or change the definitions. Roles read by a condition, including the role lists on actions that the engine folds into a condition, are reported at their condition site (for example `stage "review" activity "approve" action "approve".filter`) instead of as `generated role condition`.

  The engine now throws `UnknownProjectRolesError` (`kind: 'unknown-project-roles'`) for that rejection, carrying `projectId` and `unknown`, one entry per definition and role with every referencing path. Consumers that matched the previous plain `Error` message text should switch to the class or the `kind`.

  **No upgrade action required.** The message text changed, so anything that parsed the old per-reference lines needs updating.

  **Docs impact:** Add `UnknownProjectRolesError` to the engine error reference, and update the CLI deploy guide where it shows a failed deploy's output.

- 1d37767: `diagnoseInstance` no longer reports `progressing` when an unevaluable transition holds a stage whose activities are all resolved. This applies to every surface built on it: `workflows_diagnose` in the MCP server, the CLI `diagnose` command, and the Studio plugin's instance fault. When a transition's `when` evaluates to GROQ `null` (for example, it reads a field that hasn't been written yet) and a transition declared after it is satisfied, the engine stays in the stage until the value is written. Once every activity in the stage is resolved, the diagnosis now reports this as `stuck` with the recoverable cause `transition-unevaluable`, naming the unevaluable transitions declared before the satisfied one. When the held transition reads a referenced document that is missing, the diagnosis reports `document-missing` for that document instead, and `blockingMissingDocuments` on the evaluation lists it. Transition selection itself is unchanged. The text for this cause in `workflows_diagnose`, CLI `diagnose`, and the Studio plugin no longer promises the instance advances on its own: once the data is written, the next engine tick or commit re-checks the held transitions, and the instance advances only if a transition is then satisfied.

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact:** Update the published diagnose guidance and the `StuckCause` reference to say that, once every activity in the stage is resolved, `transition-unevaluable` is reported whenever an earlier unevaluable transition holds the stage, including when a later transition is satisfied, and that a missing document read by that held transition is reported as `document-missing`; the MCP authoring guide's transition paragraph should say the same.

- f6bcbaf: `nuke --instance` now refuses to delete an instance that is still in flight and
  tells you to abort it first. Before this fix the check never fired, so the
  command offered to delete a running instance, and `--force` deleted it without
  cancelling its pending effects or condemning its child instances.

  **No upgrade action required.** Abort a running instance with `abort` before
  deleting it with `nuke --instance`.

  **Docs impact:** None. The CLI reference already describes `nuke --instance` as
  refusing in-flight instances; this change makes the command match it.

- 816ceac: `workflows nuke --partition` now names the definitions it will delete and states the total before it asks for confirmation. Under the plan table, a `definitions:` line lists each definition name with its versions, with consecutive versions shown as a range, for example `definitions: article-review (v1–v3, v5)`. The line is omitted when the partition has no definitions. A sentence such as `This will delete 2 instances and 1 definition from partition "prod".` follows, and prints with `--force` too. That sentence and the success line after the delete now name only the document types with something to delete, joined with "and". `nuke --instance` output is unchanged.

  **No upgrade action required.** Scripts that parse nuke output should expect the two new lines.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI reference's `nuke` example output to show the `definitions:` line and the total sentence.

- f6bcbaf: `nuke` reports what it deleted in plainer words. `nuke --instance` prints
  `Deleted instance <id>.`, adding `and its guard` or `and its N guards` only
  when guards were deleted. A partition delete prints `Deleted from partition "<partition>": …`
  without the dataset count, which the plan table above it already shows. An
  empty partition reports `Nothing to delete in partition "<partition>".`

  **No upgrade action required.** Scripts that match the old `Nuked partition`
  or `guards across` wording need updating.

  **Docs impact:** None. No guide or reference quotes these lines.

- d5ecb28: What `createRuntime` keeps from `createRuntimeEngine`, what `runtime.start` requires, and the heartbeat's documented limits:
  - `runtime.engine` runs the handlers in `createRuntime`'s `effects`, as `createRuntimeEngine`'s engine ran its `effects` handlers. Its `drainEffects` fails on a pending effect the registry lacks unless `names` leaves that effect out.
  - `runtime.drain` stamps history rows and telemetry with the `drainer` execution kind, as generated drains did. `runtime.heartbeat`, `runtime.start` and `runtime.engine` stamp `server`.
  - `runtime.start` references the subject in the project and dataset that the function context's `clientOptions.projectId` and `clientOptions.dataset` name. It throws a `ContractViolationError` when either is missing. Sanity document functions always supply both.
  - The README and the `Runtime.heartbeat` reference state the heartbeat's limits: an effect becomes eligible to re-queue five minutes after it was queued, each step works on at most 30 instances per run, and the heartbeat releases expired claims. The Workflows CLI README states the same re-queue age.

  **No upgrade action required for generated functions.** A hand-written function that calls `runtime.start` with a context of its own must set `clientOptions.projectId` and `clientOptions.dataset` on it, or the start throws.

  **Docs impact:** In the generated-runtime guide, state that `runtime.engine` runs the `effects` handlers, that `runtime.start` needs the context's `projectId` and `dataset`, and that under the heartbeat an effect becomes eligible to re-queue five minutes after it was queued, each step works on at most 30 instances per run, and expired claims are released.

- effbac6: `show` no longer lists an activity as active once its run has finished. On an
  aborted or completed instance, an activity that was still open when the run
  stopped is shown dimmed as `◌ <activity>  [not finished]`, so the output still
  says where the run stopped without suggesting the work can be done. Done,
  failed, and skipped activities are shown as before.

  The section listing an instance's stages is now headed `Stage history:`. It
  lists the stages the run has entered, in order, so a stage the run has not
  reached yet does not appear and a revisited stage appears once per visit.
  `definitions show` keeps its `Stages:` heading for the workflow's full stage list.

  **No upgrade action required.** `show --json` still returns each activity's
  stored status.

  **Docs impact:** Update any CLI guide example that shows `show` output for an
  aborted or completed instance.

## 0.36.0

### Minor Changes

- 12240b6: `sanity-workflows blueprint generate` reports the runtime needs of the narrowed triggers. Each drain is listed with its own document trigger rather than one shared filter, and the start-watcher line prints the trigger the deployment compiles. The heartbeat block now says which definitions the beat ticks, which definitions' queues it recovers, how long an entry must have waited, the budget it carries and that budgeted effects recover one per beat, that a beat drains the instances it selected in sequence so a backlog continues on the next beat, and that deploying definitions before the functions loses nothing. A beat that ticks nothing and exists only to recover queues says so. A spawning action is printed as a heartbeat reason beside the `$now` deadlines, naming its stage, activity and action. The warnings change too: a start filter whose truth can change without a write to its subject is now called out with the reason and the lever, a creates-only watcher is explained under its line, and the any-type-subject warning says that every document in the dataset but the engine's own can invoke the watcher.

  Run `sanity-workflows blueprint generate` after upgrading and redeploy the blueprint: this release changes what the generator writes, so `blueprint generate --check` fails in CI until the tree is regenerated, and deployed functions keep their old wider triggers until the blueprint is redeployed. Read the new heartbeat lines while you are there, since the report is where the deployment's recovery scope and budget are stated.

  **Docs impact:** Update any walkthrough that quotes `blueprint generate` output, and the CLI reference's description of the runtime-needs report, to include the per-drain triggers, the two heartbeat scopes, the budgeted-effect rotation, and the three warning lines: the unnarrowable start filter with its lever, the creates-only explanation, and the any-type subject.

- b76d218: **BREAKING:** CLI telemetry now sends flag **values**, not just flag names.
  `extraArguments` on the `Workflows CLI Command Executed` trace carried the
  names of the flags used (`["--tag"]`); it now carries each flag in its
  canonical long form with its value (`["--tag=prod"]`). Anyone querying
  `extraArguments` for an exact flag name must match the name with or without a
  value, for example `--tag` or anything starting `--tag=`; an exact match on
  `--tag` stops counting new rows.

  `--tag=prod`, `--tag prod`, and `-t prod` all report `--tag=prod`, so a flag
  reads the same however it was typed.

  **Read this before upgrading if your deployment tags, definition names, stage
  names, or instance ids are themselves sensitive.** Values reach telemetry
  verbatim, so `--only=project-nimbus` and `--to=legal-hold` now report what
  they were set to. Who can see the data does not change, and
  `sanity telemetry disable`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, and CI suppression behave as
  before.

  Some values never ship. A flag whose value is text a person typed reports its
  name alone: `--reason` on `abort`, `set-stage`, and `definition delete`,
  `--field` on `start`, and `--param` on `fire-action`. So does any flag the
  command does not declare, including a misspelling like `--resaon`. Tokens
  after the `--` terminator are not reported.

  **Docs impact:** Update the package README's Telemetry section, which moves
  flag values to the collected list and names the redacted flags, and any
  analytics guidance that assumes Workflows CLI rows carry flag names only.

- c06a9a8: **BREAKING:** Workflows telemetry event names now all follow
  `Workflows <package> <event>`, the form the Studio plugin already uses. Every
  engine event gains `Engine` (`Workflows Instance Started` becomes
  `Workflows Engine Instance Started`). The CLI's definition-sharing events gain
  `CLI` (`Workflows CLI Definition Shared`,
  `Workflows CLI Definition Sharing Decided`), and the React session event gains
  `React` (`Workflows React Session Started`). Payloads and event versions are
  unchanged. Dashboards and queries that match the old names stop receiving new
  rows, and a telemetry logger passed to `createEngine({telemetry})` or set in
  `sanity.workflow.ts` that filters on an event name stops matching.

  Update Omni queries and dashboards to match both the old and new names until
  the old series no longer matters; rows already recorded keep their old names.
  Update any custom logger that compares `event.name` against a string. Code that
  references the exported event definitions, such as `WorkflowInstanceStarted`,
  needs no change.

  **Docs impact:** Update every telemetry reference that lists Workflows event
  names, including the engine, CLI, MCP, and React telemetry sections, and add the
  rename and the dual-name query guidance to the release notes.

- 0e072b9: `sanity-workflows deploy` now checks the generated Blueprints runtime against the definitions it is about to deploy. After the definitions validate, the deploy looks for `workflows.blueprint.ts` next to `sanity.workflow.ts`. When that file is there, the deploy runs the same comparison as `blueprint generate --check`: a regenerated shell that differs from disk, or a declared effect with no handler, exits non-zero before the first definition reaches the dataset and before a token is resolved, naming each file and the command that fixes it. When no generated runtime is there, the deploy prints the runtime the definitions need and continues; definitions needing no functions print nothing, and definitions no runtime can be derived from print a warning. `deploy --check` and `deploy --dry-run` run the check too, so `deploy --check` is a complete offline pre-flight. The deploy never writes a source file, because generation stays the explicit `blueprint generate` command.

  Teams with no generated runtime need **no upgrade action**: nothing is compared and the deploy behaves as before, apart from a report of what a generated runtime would contain. Teams that do generate one must keep it current, because a deploy now stops on drift instead of shipping definitions their runtime cannot serve: run `sanity-workflows blueprint generate`, review the result, and deploy again. The check covers the whole config, since the generated tree declares every deployment in it, so a targeted `deploy --deployment one` also stops when a sibling deployment has drifted or its definitions no longer validate. There is no flag or configuration key that turns the check off; a project that hand-writes its runtime has no generated tree for the check to compare.

  `@sanity/workflow-blueprint` exports `generatedRuntimeAlignment` from `@sanity/workflow-blueprint/generate` for callers that need that verdict themselves. It takes the directory holding the config file, reads only that directory, writes nothing, and returns the runtime the definitions need, the tree they would generate, and every planned file that differs from disk. It also takes an optional `compiler`, the TypeScript 6 compiler API used to wire an existing `sanity.blueprint.ts`; pass it when the host project's installed `typescript` package is absent or is TypeScript 7, which does not expose that API, and omit it to use the installed package. The generated resources module's own path is exported alongside it as `WORKFLOW_RESOURCES_PATH`.

  **No upgrade action required** for existing callers of `generatedRuntimeAlignment`: `compiler` is optional and omitting it preserves the prior behavior.

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI reference for `deploy`, `deploy --check`, and `deploy --dry-run` to state that the alignment check runs by default and cannot be turned off, the generated-runtime guide to describe deploy-time drift as the second gate beside the CI `blueprint generate --check` job, including the whole-config scope of a targeted deploy, and the `@sanity/workflow-blueprint` API reference for `generatedRuntimeAlignment` to document its optional `compiler` parameter.

- 3af5eb2: **BREAKING:** The `Workflows CLI Command Executed` telemetry trace is version 2
  and reports the invocation the way the Sanity CLI's own `CLI Command Executed`
  does. `groupOrCommand` is now always `workflows` rather than the full oclif id,
  and the command path moves to a new `commandArguments` array
  (`workflows:definition:list` becomes `["definition", "list"]`). The version 1
  payload fields `command` and `flags` are removed: the command path is
  `commandArguments`, and the declared flag names used are the new
  `extraArguments` array, `--`-prefixed (`["--check", "--tag"]`). A new
  `coreOptions` object reports `debug`, `help`, and `version`. All four live on
  the trace's context, so they ride every event the trace emits; `success` remains
  the only field on `trace.log`. Flag values are still never sent.

  Two audiences must act. Anyone querying Workflows CLI rows in RudderStack or
  Omni should move filters off `data.command` and `data.flags` onto the
  `Group Or Command`, `Command Arguments`, and `Extra Arguments` columns, and
  expect `Group Or Command` to read `workflows` for every Workflows row instead
  of one value per command; queries left on the old fields return nothing.
  Anyone supplying a `telemetry` logger through `sanity.workflow.ts` receives the
  new field set on the same event name — a logger that reads `command` or `flags`
  must read `commandArguments` and `extraArguments` instead, or it will record
  `undefined`.

  **Docs impact:** The package README's Telemetry section documents this event
  field by field; its `Workflows CLI Command Executed` entry is updated here to
  the version 2 context and payload. Any dashboard or analytics guidance that
  names `data.command` or `data.flags` needs the same correction.

## 0.35.0

### Minor Changes

- a3489d2: Workflows CLI commands now load `sanity.workflow.ts` in projects using
  TypeScript 7. `blueprint generate` and `blueprint generate --check` work with
  TypeScript 6, TypeScript 7, or no project TypeScript installation: the CLI
  supplies its own TypeScript 6 compatibility compiler for editing an existing
  `sanity.blueprint.ts`. Direct generator callers can pass that API through
  `emissionWritePlan({compiler})` or as the second argument to `wireBlueprint`.
  When no usable compiler is available, direct wiring reports how to supply one.
  The Blueprint package root now exports `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES` so custom loaders
  can share the same config discovery order without importing the generator.
  The workflow engine and generated function runtimes do not acquire a compiler
  dependency.

  **No upgrade action required.** Install the updated Workflows release normally;
  keep your project's TypeScript version and existing config files.

  **Docs impact:** Update the Blueprint generation reference to explain the
  optional compiler argument and root `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES` export for direct
  callers, and the CLI installation guidance to say Blueprint commands work in
  projects using TypeScript 6, TypeScript 7, or no installed TypeScript.

### Patch Changes

- 2f040b6: The README's Telemetry section now states the payload policy as an explicit
  collected / never-collected pair, governed by
  [Sanity's telemetry policy](https://www.sanity.io/telemetry), replacing the
  claim that payloads never include customer-authored strings. That claim was
  wrong in three ways it is worth knowing about: the dataset name is sent as a
  session property, effect events carry the author-chosen effect name, and the
  deployment tag reaches telemetry inside `instanceId`, whose engine-minted form
  is `<tag>.wf-instance.<random>`. A caller-supplied instance id is sent
  verbatim. Nothing about what the CLI sends changes; only the description of it
  does.

  The never-collected list now separates what the company policy excludes from
  what this package additionally chooses not to send. Flag values, definition
  names, and stage names sit in the second group: the policy does not prohibit
  them, so do not read their absence here as a company-wide guarantee. Error
  messages sit there too, with the policy permitting error information that
  excludes sensitive data while this package sends none.

  **No upgrade action required.** Review the new lists if you assessed this
  package's telemetry against the previous wording, in particular if your
  deployment tags or instance ids encode something you would not want in an
  analytics pipeline. Consent and opt-out are unchanged: account-level
  `sanity telemetry disable`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, and CI suppression all behave as
  before.

  **Docs impact:** The Telemetry section of the package README is the change.
  Any internal analytics or privacy guidance quoting the old
  "never include customer-authored strings" sentence needs the same correction,
  and guidance that assumes deployment tags are absent from telemetry should be
  revisited.

## 0.33.0

### Minor Changes

- 225e0fb: **BREAKING:** Workflows App SDK and Studio integrations now require `@sanity/sdk` 3.1 or later in the 3.x line, and `@sanity/workflow-sdk` requires the matching `@sanity/sdk-react` 3.1 line when its React entry is used. The previous SDK 2 peer contract is no longer supported. The exported `WorkflowClient`, `TelemetryIntakeClient`, `ProjectUserProfileClient`, and `StudioUserClient` request contracts now pass their target in `url`; the previous `uri` request target is no longer used. The engine's effective client config also accepts the broader `{type: string, id: string}` resource descriptors returned by Sanity client 8.

  Before upgrading Workflows, upgrade `@sanity/sdk` and `@sanity/sdk-react` together to 3.1 or later. Applications that stay on SDK 2 must stay on an earlier Workflows release. If you implement any of the request contracts named above, update it to read the request target from `url` instead of `uri`; otherwise its request-backed reads will fail. Existing `WorkflowClient.config()` implementations need no change when their resource descriptor already has string `type` and `id` fields. No separate CLI upgrade action is required; its definition-sharing and telemetry requests adopt `url` internally.

  Before installing, override SDK 3's `@sanity/mutate` dependency to `0.18.2` in your application's root package-manager configuration, reinstall, and commit the updated lockfile. SDK 3.1.0 allows Mutate 0.18.1, which can leave document reads pending with client 8. For npm, set `overrides["@sanity/sdk"]["@sanity/mutate"]` to `"0.18.2"` in `package.json`. For pnpm, set `overrides['@sanity/sdk@3>@sanity/mutate']` to `0.18.2` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Keep the override until your SDK release requires Mutate 0.18.2 or later. Complete examples and verification steps are in the Installation section of the published `@sanity/workflow-sdk` README.

  Malformed project-member responses now report an inaccessible directory and can recover on a later lookup, instead of being cached as a missing user. No additional upgrade action is required for this correction.

  **Docs impact:** Update the App SDK and Studio integration installation guidance, package compatibility references, and examples to require Sanity App SDK 3.1 and the consumer Mutate override described in the published `@sanity/workflow-sdk` README; update the client API references for `request({url})`, effective resource descriptors, and directory-response failures.

- ba031fe: **Experimental, and not ready for production use in this release.** Both commands are available so you can try the generated runtime and give feedback; their flags and their output may still change. What you would hit today:
  - The start watcher runs on every create and update of a subject type, not only on writes that can actually start a workflow, so it wakes for documents that already have an instance or match no definition. The heartbeat is scheduled every minute and evaluates every in-flight instance in the tag when it runs; how often the platform runs it is a plan limit.
  - `sanity-workflows deploy` does not check the generated tree, so drift between your definitions and the tree on disk is caught only by `blueprint generate --check` in CI.
  - Definitions and functions deploy in two steps, definitions first, until the Blueprints service registers the `sanity.workflow` resource.
  - A generated file cannot be taken over: editing one is drift, and the next generation rewrites it.
  - A retry policy is not checked against its function's timeout at generation, so an effect can be configured to retry for longer than its function may run.

  All of these are tracked, and the next release is the bar for using this in production.

  `sanity-workflows blueprint generate` generates the Sanity Blueprints runtime your definitions require and writes it next to `sanity.workflow.ts`. It prints the needs analysis first — which effects force a drain function, which `$now` condition forces a scheduled heartbeat, which autonomous definition forces a start watcher, and the explicit "no functions needed" answer for a purely interactive workflow — then writes `workflows.blueprint.ts`, one function module and manifest per derived need, the effect-handler registry, and one handler stub per declared effect name. Handler stubs are yours: they are scaffolded once and never overwritten. Your own `sanity.blueprint.ts` receives the `workflowResources` import and spread once. The command deletes nothing; a handler for an effect you removed, a scaffold blocked by a path differing only in case, and a blueprint it could not wire are reported as warnings for you to resolve. The generated tree is one artifact for the whole config, so the command always covers every deployment.

  `sanity-workflows blueprint generate --check` is the CI drift gate. It renders the same runtime in memory, compares it with the files on disk, writes nothing, and exits zero when they match. Otherwise it exits 1 and lists every file with its reason — `missing`, `differs`, an orphaned handler, or a blueprint that is not wired — so a CI log says what to fix without anyone reading source. A declared effect with no handler file on disk reports as `missing`, which is the handler-coverage check.

  **No upgrade action required.** Both commands are new and nothing else changes. To use them, your `sanity.workflow.ts` must export each deployment under its own `name`, and that export must be the deployment object itself — `export const production = {name: 'production', …} satisfies WorkflowDeploymentInput`, then `export default defineWorkflowConfig({deployments: [production]})` — because every generated module imports its deployment from `./sanity.workflow` by that name; a config that only default-exports fails the command with the export to add rather than writing a tree that cannot compile. The command checks the name only, so make sure each export is the deployment the config lists: a typecheck of the generated modules catches a wrong export only where a generated function uses it, and a deployment that needs no functions emits none. Your `sanity.workflow.ts` must also be importable inside a deployed function, because every generated module imports it and each function bundles it: reading an absent variable there yields `undefined`, but a config that throws when a variable is missing, or requires one to build the deployment, fails every deployed function on init. Keep the deployment's resource coordinates literal in that file and read secrets inside your handlers. Deploy your definitions with `sanity-workflows deploy` before `npx sanity blueprints deploy`, because the generated blueprint carries the definitions entry commented out until the Blueprints service accepts the `sanity.workflow` resource type, and a function that starts or advances an instance resolves its definition from the Content Lake. A generated heartbeat is a scheduled function, which the platform only accepts on an organization-scoped stack, and how often it may run is a plan limit. Also install `@sanity/blueprints`, `@sanity/functions`, and `@sanity/workflow-blueprint` in your project: each generated function's manifest copies the specifications your project declares for `@sanity/functions`, `@sanity/workflow-blueprint`, and `@sanity/workflow-engine`, and a package you declare nowhere fails the command instead of being stamped with a guessed range. `typescript` is now a dependency of the CLI, because parsing `sanity.blueprint.ts` to insert the wiring uses the TypeScript compiler.

  **Docs impact:** Rewrite the cookbook chapter on running workflows on a server so it drives the runtime through these two commands rather than describing hand-written functions, and cover the CI drift check there. Update the CLI command reference with both commands, and the Blueprints concept page where it explains who writes the generated tree.

### Patch Changes

- 393ac71: CLI and MCP telemetry now includes `context.surface` (`cli` or `mcp`) and
  execution mode in each event's `context.environment`. Dashboards can include
  shell and engine activity while distinguishing it from SDK events marked
  `sdk`. Existing command trace context is preserved.

  All three surfaces report `production` for `NODE_ENV=production`, and
  `development` for `development` or `test`. Unset, empty, and unrecognized values
  default to `production` for CLI and MCP execution mode, and `development` for
  SDK build mode. SDK environment classification is unchanged. When comparing
  activity across surfaces, group or filter by surface alongside environment.
  Environment does not identify a production dataset or deployment; API host,
  dataset name, and workflow tag do not set it.

  **No upgrade action required.** Existing telemetry consent and opt-out
  settings still apply. Historical events are unchanged.

  **Docs impact:** Update CLI, MCP, and SDK telemetry guidance to explain surface
  context, build versus execution mode, the explicit defaults, and how to
  interpret environment when comparing activity across surfaces.

- 8874c50: **BREAKING:** A `subject`, `doc.ref`, or `doc.refs` field marked `required: true`
  now requires its selected documents to remain readable after initialization.
  Previously, the flag checked only that an initial value was supplied. Missing
  required targets now produce a fault and prevent normal actions, triggered
  actions, and transitions from advancing, even without an activity requirement
  reading those targets. Abort and direct edits to editable fields remain
  available. Optional references fault only when an unmet runtime condition needs
  their content; completed workflows remain completed.

  `StuckCause` adds `document-missing`. Update exhaustive handlers before upgrading,
  or their typechecks fail and renderers have no matching branch. Evaluation
  identifies the affected field and reference in `missingDocuments`, with its title
  and completed availability evidence; `blockingMissingDocuments` selects the
  references that prevent progress. The engine checks draft, published, and release
  representations before distinguishing deletion from inaccessible content or
  content outside the workflow perspective. Studio, CLI, and MCP use that same
  result. Failed availability checks report unreadable content and log the cause;
  optional references still permit unrelated actions. Incomplete reads do not
  claim deletion, and an existing task fault keeps
  its recovery controls. The fault clears when the required content becomes
  readable; this release adds no undo-delete operation and does not automatically
  abort workflows.

  Upgrade every Workflows runtime sharing affected data, including Studio, CLI,
  MCP servers, and deployed Functions, before relying on continued required-target
  availability. Then set the deployment's reviewed `expectedMinReaderModel` to
  `10` before deploying definitions with required content references. Writers stamp
  model 10; this feature requires reader model 10, while documents without it keep
  the floor required by their other features, normally 4, 8, or 9. Existing
  instances remain readable without a backfill and adopt the rule under upgraded
  engines. Their stored floor rises on the next full write, so an older runtime
  can still advance an unstamped existing instance until the fleet is upgraded.
  See `packages/workflow-engine/DATAMODEL.md` for the complete rollout contract.

  The rendered CLI `show` command evaluates running instances. If evaluation fails,
  it warns and displays stored state; terminal instances and `show --json` retain
  their stored-state behavior.

  **Docs impact:** Update field requiredness and initialization guidance, required
  reference repair examples, the model-10 readers-first rollout, the diagnostics
  reference for `StuckCause` and `MissingDocument`, CLI `show` and `diagnose`, MCP
  workflow-state guidance, and the Workflows tool and document-view guides for
  loading, deletion, permissions, and perspectives.

- 3b42bdc: The Workflows CLI command-trace now sets the oclif command id as trace context (`groupOrCommand`) when the built-in telemetry shell starts, so telemetry reporting can break invocations down by command the same way it can for other Sanity CLI commands. The id remains in the log payload as `command` for config-provided telemetry loggers.

  **No upgrade action required.** Existing CLI installs begin emitting the queryable context after upgrading; historical rows are unchanged.

  **Docs impact:** None — internal telemetry envelope shape for an existing event; no public API or user-facing CLI behavior change.

- 7eb9eca: Correct the API references for field initialization and edits, start requirements,
  transitions, reference IDs, effect handling, reactive state, member controls,
  Studio mappings, test helpers, and GROQ condition outcomes. The references state
  caller constraints and defaults that were missing or incorrect. Package setup
  guidance identifies the public npm packages and supported deployment command;
  the MCP validation description distinguishes validation from deployment checks.
  Runtime behavior and API signatures are unchanged.

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact:** After release and reference sync, reconcile the modeling,
  runtime, reactive UI, Studio, testing, deployment, MCP, and evaluation-insight
  guides and references with the corrected contracts. Fix affected examples and
  replace redundant API inventories with verified symbol links while preserving
  useful teaching and the CLI/MCP reference material not exposed by TypeDoc.

- 2cef086: Internal maintenance consolidates engine action/edit handling and Studio document
  and workflow title sorting. Action and field-edit calls retain their inputs and
  results, and document and workflow titles retain their ordering. Action
  availability, telemetry, and persisted document formats are unchanged.

  **No upgrade action required.**

  **Docs impact: None** because public APIs, configuration, and workflow behavior
  are unchanged.

## 0.32.0

### Minor Changes

- a8ed312: **BREAKING:** Assignment is now one ordered user-or-role member-list model: a direct user holder shadows every role in the same activity, role-only values route work to a pool, and singular `assignee` fields allow at most one user while retaining any number of roles. The `claim` field and action sugars have been removed from the authoring DSL; authors using them must replace each pair with an `assignee` field, a literal role seed where the work starts in a pool, ordinary field edits for take/release, a guarded `editable` predicate when second-taker exclusion is required, and `$assigned` on holder-only actions. Definitions that still submit `type: 'claim'` now fail validation.

  Upgrade every engine, Studio, CLI, MCP, and adapter runtime sharing a workflow resource before deploying a definition containing a singular `assignee`, then acknowledge reader model 9 on deployment. Existing model-8-and-earlier instances remain readable and keep their object/null singular representation; no stored-document backfill is required. Deploy now rejects project-role references absent from the target project's live role catalog and warns when a referenced role has no current human holder, so the deploying identity must be able to read the project role and member directories.

  Studio assignment matching and holder explanations now follow direct-user shadowing. The CLI adds viewer-scoped assignment list flags and counts, MCP instance listing adds corresponding assignment inputs and counts, and the public waiting `Diagnosis` adds a required `waitingFor` discriminant that distinguishes caller-actionable, manual-but-unavailable, and automation waits without implying that unassigned work is freely actionable.

  `@sanity/workflow-components` now exports `roleMemberCount`, which reports the distinct people who can fulfill any supplied project role using the workflow definition's aliases. Pass the current member directory, required role names, and normalized `roleAliases`; literal members and alias-only fulfillers are deduplicated by account-global user id. No upgrade action is required unless a custom assignment surface wants alias-aware pool sizes.

  **Docs impact:** Update the assignment model and authoring references, the reader-model rollout guide, guarded role-pool and take/release examples, the `@sanity/workflow-components` member-selection reference for `roleMemberCount`, Studio task-holder explanations, CLI instance-list flags, MCP list tool reference, deploy role-validation requirements, and migration guidance from removed claim sugar.

### Patch Changes

- 8fc1f36: `@sanity/cli-core` is now a peer dependency, which reduces the install size of `@sanity/cli`

  **No upgrade action required.** The peer dependency isn't marked optional, so package managers will still install it like normal.

  **Docs impact:** None.

- f1c9446: The CLI now formats timestamps with `@sanity/cli-core` instead of installing `date-fns`, reducing the standalone installation size while preserving absolute detail timestamps and relative list timestamps.

  **No upgrade action required.** Relative timestamps use the runtime's standard English wording.

  **Docs impact:** None. Timestamp presentation and CLI usage remain unchanged.

## 0.30.0

### Minor Changes

- 90207dc: **BREAKING:** `assertReaderModelAcknowledgement` now requires `{requiredMinReaderModel, context?}` instead of a context string, and `ReaderModelAcknowledgementError` accepts its optional context through `{context}`. The Blueprint package's `AcknowledgedDeployment` type moves to the engine as `AcknowledgedWorkflowDeployment`; update imports and use that shared name. Assignment-valued fields can now declare a non-empty `roles` list that limits newly written assignees. Existing fields without `roles` stay unconstrained, retain reader floor 4, and continue deploying with `expectedMinReaderModel: 4`; installing this release requires no coordinated rollout or configuration change.

  Before adding `roles`, upgrade every Studio, CLI, MCP server, Function, and other runtime that shares the affected workflow resource, then change that deployment's literal `expectedMinReaderModel` to `8`. MCP deployments pass the same reviewed literal as the optional `expectedMinReaderModel` tool argument. Definitions and instances carrying the facet require reader model 8. User assignees qualify through direct roles or the definition's role aliases, while collective role assignees must literally match one configured role. Studio assignment controls, including manual start, auto-start, and assignees nested in to-do rows, offer only eligible choices while retaining stale current values so editors can remove or replace them. Constrained pickers name the active eligible roles and distinguish an empty eligible set from a search with no matches. Top-level plural and composite edits retain no more occurrences of a stale assignment at each declared assignment location than the previous value contained; removal and reordering therefore work, while an added copy is a new assignment and must qualify. Direct singular replacements and every assignment present in an `updateWhere` fragment remain strict. Each engine verb uses one member-directory snapshot across retries, cascade hops, and spawned children, then the next verb reads current membership.

  Malformed project-member and project-user directory responses now fail loudly instead of treating bad rows or role records as missing users, and actor resolution reports those failures as `inaccessible`, so integrations can distinguish directory failures from absent membership.

  CLI `start` and `definition delete` no longer apply the definition-submission acknowledgement gate; deploy, check, dry-run, definition diff, Blueprint provision, and engine definition APIs still validate the selected definitions' required floor.

  No reader-fleet rollout or deployment-literal change is required for existing definitions that do not use `roles`.

  **Docs impact:** Update the assignment field reference and authoring examples for `roles`, distinguish eligibility from editability, action permission, and literal queue ownership, and add the model-8 conditional adoption sequence to the prerelease rollout guide.

- b0b1550: **BREAKING:** Product-prefixed telemetry events now use `Workflows <event>` instead of `Editorial Workflows <event>`; `EditorialWorkflowsResource` is replaced by `WorkflowsResource`; and `defineWorkflows` now generates `workflows-<deployment name>` resource names instead of `editorial-workflows-<deployment name>`. Telemetry consumers matching the previous literals stop receiving events until updated, TypeScript consumers importing the previous Blueprint interface no longer compile, and an existing Blueprint stack that relies on the generated name treats the new default as a different resource identity.

  Update telemetry dashboards, schemas, alerts, and queries to match the `Workflows` prefix; event suffixes, payloads, and versions are unchanged. Replace Blueprint imports with `WorkflowsResource`. Before deploying an existing Blueprint stack, either pass its recorded resource name explicitly or plan the detach-and-create migration to the new default. Workflows request-tag families and billing classification are unchanged.

  Other user-facing package copy now uses the Workflows product name. No upgrade action is required for consumers that do not match telemetry event names or use the Blueprint package.

  **Docs impact:** Rename the product throughout the public documentation, move the docs section to `/docs/workflows/*` with permanent redirects from every `/docs/editorial-workflows/*` path, and document the telemetry-prefix, `WorkflowsResource`, and Blueprint resource-name migrations in the telemetry reference, Blueprint guide, and release notes.

## 0.28.0

### Minor Changes

- 5050b06: **BREAKING:** Authoring a deployment now types through `WorkflowDeploymentInput` / `WorkflowConfigInput`, which require `expectedMinReaderModel` as the current reader-floor literal. Passing a parsed `WorkflowDeployment` / `WorkflowConfig` (where the floor is optional/unverified) into `defineWorkflowConfig` or `defineWorkflows` is a type error — share the authored deployment object instead of `config.deployments[n]`. The same pin shows up on the blueprint resource: `EditorialWorkflowsResource.deployment` and `parseWorkflowDeployment`'s return type are now `AcknowledgedDeployment` (floor asserted to the current literal), so a hand-constructed provider resource must carry that literal too.

  At runtime, config parse no longer rejects a stale or missing floor on an untargeted deployment. Only deployment-scoped commands assert, and only the selected deployment: definition deploy, `--check` / `--dry-run`, blueprint provision, `start`, `definition delete`, and `definition diff` (the last is a deployment-scoped read). Instance-id commands (`fire-action`, `abort`, `set-stage`, `reset-activity`) deliberately do not assert — they resolve by instance id, not by a declared deployment's acknowledgement — so an unacknowledged floor does not stop those instance commits.

  Upgrade TypeScript configs and blueprint manifests that fed a parsed deployment into those helpers: keep a shared authored object (`satisfies WorkflowDeploymentInput`) for both `defineWorkflowConfig` and `defineWorkflows`, and give any hand-built `EditorialWorkflowsResource` the current floor literal on `deployment`. Existing configs that already acknowledge the current floor keep working at runtime; a stale selected deployment still fails with `ReaderModelAcknowledgementError` (headline + short steps; the CLI renders it through the clean styled-error path).

  **Docs impact:** Update the CLI / blueprint authoring examples and the prerelease reader-floor guidance so they name `WorkflowConfigInput` / `WorkflowDeploymentInput` / `AcknowledgedDeployment`, forbid passing `config.deployments[n]` into `defineWorkflows`, state that instance-id writes are outside the acknowledgement gate, and stop implying whole-config parse-time rejection for commands that never select a deployment.

- cc50d58: **BREAKING:** Canonical oclif command ids move from the `editorial-workflows` topic to `workflows`. A future host mount therefore surfaces `sanity workflows deploy` (and the same shape for every other command) instead of `sanity editorial-workflows …`. Standalone short forms (`sanity-workflows deploy`, `definition list`, …) are unchanged — the bin still rewrites them onto the topic before resolution.

  Anyone invoking the previous topic-scoped ids (`sanity-workflows editorial-workflows deploy`, or a host/plugin that hard-coded those ids) must switch to `workflows …`. Continuing to call `editorial-workflows …` fails with command-not-found.

  **Docs impact:** When the host mount ships, update Editorial Workflows CLI getting-started and invocation docs so the documented host path is `sanity workflows …`, and refresh any topic-scoped examples that still say `editorial-workflows`. Until then the standalone short forms remain the documented surface.

### Patch Changes

- 4403e66: Short command forms (`deploy`, `definition list`, …) are no longer registered as oclif root aliases. The standalone `sanity-workflows` binary still accepts those forms by rewriting argv onto the `workflows` topic before command resolution, so day-to-day usage is unchanged. Removing the aliases makes the package safe to mount inside the official `sanity` CLI without colliding with host commands such as `sanity deploy`.

  **No upgrade action required** for standalone `sanity-workflows` / `npx @sanity/workflow-cli` users. Anyone who embedded this package as an oclif plugin and relied on the root aliases must invoke the topic-scoped ids (`workflows deploy`, …) or perform equivalent argv rewriting in the host.

  **Docs impact:** Update Editorial Workflows CLI getting-started and invocation docs when the host mount ships so the primary path is `sanity workflows …`; until then the standalone short forms remain the documented surface in this package README.

## 0.25.0

### Minor Changes

- 177d600: Deployed workflow environment tags are now discoverable.

  The engine gains two cross-partition GROQ builders: `deployedTagsGroq()` lists
  every tag holding a deployed definition in a resource, and
  `definitionTagsGroq()` narrows that to one definition name via `$definition`.
  Both deliberately span tag partitions — every other read is tag-scoped, and
  `workflow.query` refuses GROQ that isn't — so they answer "which environments
  exist here" for a caller holding a resource but no tag. They report what is
  _observed_: a tag with nothing deployed does not appear.

  The stdio MCP server adds a `list_workflow_tags` tool taking a
  `workflow_resource` and no tag. It is registered by the host rather than exported
  as a tool def, because a def is only ever handed an engine and an engine is
  pinned to one tag. `LIST_WORKFLOW_TAGS_TOOL_NAME` and
  `LIST_WORKFLOW_TAGS_DESCRIPTION` are exported so an embedding host registers the
  same capability under the same name without re-authoring the model-facing
  wording. The `tag` parameter's description now points an agent at that tool where
  a server offers it and at the user otherwise, and requires confirmation either
  way — having the list does not license picking from it.

  Both registration paths share one outcome path, `withToolTelemetry`, so the
  result envelope, error rendering, and the `Editorial Workflows MCP Tool Called`
  event cannot diverge between a def-backed tool and a host-registered one. Tag
  discovery reports its adoption event like every other tool, and because it names
  a resource it can also initialize the stdio server's deferred telemetry shell —
  which matters when discovery is an agent's first call.

  The CLI's definition-tags probe runs the engine's builder instead of its own
  copy of the query, so its `params` key is `definition` rather than `name`, and
  the tag partitions it names in an ambiguity error arrive sorted from the lake.

## 0.24.0

### Minor Changes

- e359f4b: Add `nuke --instance <id>`: delete a single terminal workflow instance and its guard documents (swept across every alias-bound resource), instead of wiping a whole deployment tag. In-flight instances are refused — abort them first, and so is any document that is not an engine instance, so a bare id can never reach co-located content. Prints a dry-run plan, then a `y/N` confirmation (`--force` skips it).

  Instance mode locates its target by lake-side projection rather than a gated engine read, so it can delete an instance whose reader floor is ahead of the running engine — the state the reset exists to clear, and which tag mode could already handle.

  Instance mode deletes the instance document in its LAST wave, after the guards. A nuke is never a single transaction, so an interrupted run always leaves something behind — and that document is the handle a re-run locates by, so deleting it first would strand any guard the run had not yet reached with nothing left to name them. Tag mode keeps deleting instance documents first, unchanged: it re-plans from a query, so a re-run sweeps whatever survived either way.

### Patch Changes

- fc02505: `deploy --only` now fails fast: the definition name is checked against the config before any deployment is selected, so a bogus value errors immediately instead of after the interactive deployment picker has been answered. When the value names a deployment rather than a definition, the failure points at the flag it belongs to — `"review-prod" is a deployment — did you mean --deployment review-prod?`.

- 795b4bb: `set-stage` now makes `--to` optional: omit it on an interactive terminal and the command presents a picker of the instance's declared stages, with the current stage marked and the cursor opened on it. ## 0.22.0

### Minor Changes

- 1c6d4c0: Name the target deployment and resource on `deploy` progress and result lines. The spinner and completion line now read `Deploying N definition(s) to <name> (<tag>) → <resource>…` / `Processed N definition(s) · <name> (<tag>) → <resource>` (and the dry-run equivalents), so a single-deployment run — the common case, which prints no per-batch banner — always shows where the deploy landed.
- fb42001: The instance-keyed commands — `diagnose`, `fire-action`, `set-stage`, `abort`, `reset-activity` — now locate an instance by fanning out across every configured resource, the same way `show` and the other read commands already do. Passing an instance id is enough: on a config that spans several resources they no longer prompt for (or require) a `--deployment` / `--tag` selector — those stay as optional narrowers. As an optimization, an id carrying the engine's default `<tag>.` mint prefix probes that tag's resource first and skips the fan-out on a hit. `reset-activity` also gains the `--deployment` narrower its siblings already had.
- 84ff807: The read commands — `list`, `show`, `definition list`, `definition show` — now take `--json`, emitting structured output on stdout for parity with the verb commands. `show` and `definition show` print the fetched document as stored; `list` and `definition list` print their table's row view (each row annotated with the `resource` it came from) under a `truncated` flag. A JSON read spanning several resources is all-or-nothing: an unreadable resource fails the whole command rather than emitting a partial listing a script would mistake for the complete result.

### Minor Changes

## 0.14.0

### Minor Changes

- 59b40fd: **BREAKING:** deployment selection now keys on the deployment `name`, selected with `--deployment`. Deployment-targeted commands (`start`, `definition diff`, `definition delete`, `nuke`) take `--deployment` as the precise selector; `--tag` still selects while it names exactly one deployment and errors listing the candidates when it spans several. `deploy --tag <tag>` now deploys every deployment carrying the tag (a tag is an environment group); `--deployment` deploys one, `--all-tags` deploys everything, and the three are mutually exclusive. `nuke` requires exactly one of `--deployment` / `--tag`, and refuses when another same-tag deployment sweeps an overlapping resource — guard document ids embed only the tag, so within a shared dataset the sweep cannot tell the deployments' guards apart and would delete the other's live locks. The interactive deploy prompt selects by name with the tag as its description. Read commands keep `--tag` as an optional filter — a repeated tag fans reads out across every resource it is deployed to.
- de7ccfa: The instance-keyed commands (`diagnose`, `abort`, `set-stage`, `fire-action`) accept `--deployment <name>` to choose which resource to read the instance from — the precise selector consistent with the deployment-targeted commands. `--deployment` names one deployment and reads from the resource it targets; `--tag` stays the optional narrower it was, and the instance's own tag partition still comes from the loaded instance itself, never from the flag. This closes the dead end where a tag repeated across several resources left these commands unable to resolve a resource, and the "spans multiple resources" failures now point at `--deployment` as the remedy.
